kplotly.r

Site: https://kbosirany.github.io/kplotly.r/ (development version: /dev)

An interactive plot with several series, a shared legend and a range slider quickly costs a dozen lines of plot_ly() / add_trace() / layout() calls and long-format bookkeeping. kplotly.r draws a complete interactive plot in one short call, and plots stay composable through the kplotly S3 class. It is the plotly.js counterpart of kggplot, with the same arguments: changing kggplot( into kplotly( turns a static plot into an interactive one.

plotly.js is embedded (the “cartesian” bundle): kplotly.r only depends on htmlwidgets, not on the plotly R package and its dependencies.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("kbosirany/kplotly.r")

Example 

library(kplotly.r)

# A time series: several columns, a range slider and a unified hover
weather <- data.frame(date = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:364)
weather$rain <- rgamma(365, 0.4, 0.1)
weather$temp <- 12 + 8 * sin(1:365 / 58 - 1.5)
kplotly(weather, "date", c("rain", "temp"), title = "Weather")

# kplot / TSstudio style calls
kplotly(weather, vars = list(x = "date", y = "all"), type = "point")

# Superpose layers: shared colours, one legend entry per level
obs <- data.frame(t = 1:20, v = (1:20)^1.2 + rnorm(20))
sim <- data.frame(t = 1:20, v = (1:20)^1.2)
kplotly(obs, "t", "v", color = "Observed", type = "point", theme = "inrae") +
  kplotly(sim, "t", "v", color = "Simulated", type = "line")

# Any plotly.js layout attribute, and the htmlwidget for Shiny
p <- kplotly(iris, "Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", color = "Species") |>
  kply_layout(hovermode = "x")
as_htmlwidget(p)

See vignette("kplotly") (“Get started”) for the full tour.

Branch, version and release conventions are those of kpkg.r: vignette("workflow", package = "kpkg.r").
